A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LiCE research. All 31 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: V2 reports original counterfactual-generation experiments on GMSC, Adult, and German Credit, including success rates, quality measurements, variant comparisons, and runtimes.

after.justification: V3 retains original experiments on the same datasets and reports revised success rates, counterfactual quality, variant comparisons, and runtimes.

M1.justification: The SPN encoding, classifier encoding, and counterfactual-generation procedures remain unchanged. The likelihood term incorporated into v3 Eq. 13 was already defined in v2 Appendix A.2.1, Eq. 14, and tested with alpha = 0.1 in Appendix A.5.2. Its promotion to the main text is not a new method.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate counterfactual explanations for the same neural-network classification tasks on GMSC, Adult, and German Credit. No dataset, domain, or distinct test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: The baseline suite remains DiCE, VAE, C-CHVAE, FACE with epsilon and knn variants, PROPLACE, and MIO. No baseline is selectively added or removed from a retained comparison. Changes to LiCE variants and deletion of the entire common-factual analysis concern ablation coverage.

E3.justification: V3 removes the auxiliary evaluation restricted to common successful factuals: 12 GMSC, 64 Adult, and 54 Credit instances in v2 Table 9. Success-rate and timing comparisons also replace quartile LiCE with optimizing LiCE. The core five-fold evaluation, 500 factuals per dataset, preprocessing, classifier, metrics, and 120-second solver budget remain as stated.

E4.justification: V2 Appendix A.5.1 and Table 9 analyze all methods on shared factuals to address differences in their successful evaluation subsets; this entire control analysis disappears. The LiCE variant study also drops the sample-dependent threshold ablation. V3 Table 9 corresponds to v2 Table 10, retaining optimize, quartile, and median variants rather than introducing a new ablation.

E5.justification: Both versions describe five-fold cross-validation and report means with standard deviations for counterfactual quality. Neither adds seeds, repeated-run information, confidence intervals, significance tests, or a different uncertainty-estimation practice.

E6.justification: MIO/LiCE results are extensively revised while external baseline scores remain unchanged. Table 2 changes GMSC median-LiCE validity from 3.2% to 53.6%; Table 3 changes its Credit NLL from 47.4 ± 18.3 to 30.5 ± 3.2. Median-LiCE GMSC runtime changes from 1851.30 to 122.27 seconds. Shared-factual and sample-variant results disappear. These are reported revisions, not established same-sample performance gains, since successful subsets change and the underlying revisions are unexplained.

T1.justification: The SPN approximation bound, assumptions, and mathematical constraint formulations remain unchanged. Integrating v2's existing weighted objective into v3 Eq. 13 and renumbering appendix equations introduce no new derivation, theorem, or proof.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: encoding SPNs in MIO and generating plausible, close, sparse counterfactuals satisfying common constraints. The changed experimental discussion does not redefine these contributions.

C2.justification: Section 5 changes the likelihood interpretation from comparable performance to best performance for the proposed methods. Appendix A.5 changes the runtime interpretation from a broad LiCE disadvantage to comparability on Adult and Credit, and attributes optimizing LiCE's delay mainly to proving optimality. The explanation based on common-factual comparisons is removed.

D1.justification: V3 removes the documented recipe for the omitted sample-threshold configuration: bounding likelihood by the smaller of the factual's likelihood and the training median. Retained implementation libraries, hyperparameters, hardware, preprocessing, and code/data-access information are unchanged. Alpha = 0.1 was already disclosed in v2.

R1.justification: Table 1 changes the attribution of sparsity from FACE to DiCE, a limited revision to the characterization of prior methods. The bibliography, related-work discussion, and principal novelty positioning otherwise remain unchanged.

P1.justification: V3 brings the existing likelihood-optimization explanation into Section 4, locally rewrites experimental interpretations, and reorganizes Appendix A.5. Most prose and section structure remain intact. The revised appendix introduces an unfinished sentence and explicit editorial placeholders.

P2.justification: The common-factual results table is removed, while the variant and runtime tables are relocated, renumbered, and have their rows revised. Table 3 adds downward arrows and explains that lower values are better. Figure 1 and the overall visual format remain unchanged.

improvement.justification: V3 makes the two existing LiCE objectives clearer in the main text, but removes the shared-factual comparison that addressed the acknowledged difficulty of comparing methods on different successful subsets. It also leaves unfinished editorial notes in Appendix A.5 and a timing caption referring to the Credit time limit despite newly reported subsecond results. These losses in evidential support and editorial consistency outweigh the limited clarity gains; more favorable reported numbers alone do not establish improved paper quality.
